get.summary: Every pack this Realm can resolve a category from.

post.summary: Register one profile pack alongside the compiled seeds.
post.description:
Admin, because it widens what every later `epics:apply` in this Realm may
freeze onto a task.

# Idempotency

It takes an `Idempotency-Key` like every other write on this surface. A
receipt cannot carry it — a receipt is written against a project and a
realm-scoped catalogue has none — so the key is bound, once and permanently,
to a **fingerprint of this logical operation**: a digest over the operation
name, the pack, its revision and its content, canonicalized exactly the way a
command intent is.

Three answers, and no fourth:

* same key, same fingerprint → the original answer, `unchanged`;
* same key, same `(pack_id, version)`, different bytes → `409`;
* same key reused for a *different* pack, revision or content → `409`, the
  key is already bound to another logical operation.

Binding to a fingerprint rather than to the pack alone is what makes the
third case refusable. Content immutability answers "may these bytes be this
revision?" and cannot answer "was this key already used for something else?",
because two registrations of two different packs are each independently
valid and nothing would be comparing them.

400.description: The pack document does not validate

409.description: This revision is registered with different content

post.summary: Record one control-plane command intent.
post.description:
The kind, the target and the desired state are checked against the domain's own
compatibility matrix before anything is written, and the revision is checked
against what the aggregate currently stands at — so a caller working from a
stale read is told the current revision and nothing is mutated. The write
itself is `kontor-store`'s single transaction: intent, target row, outbox
entry, first durable transition, desired state and the intent event, or none of
them.

409.description: Stale revision or a reused idempotency key

post.summary: Resolve a context-window policy from explicit inputs, and change nothing.
post.description:
A pure read: it touches no store, dispatches to no runtime and persists
nothing, so asking "what would this seat get" is free of consequence. The
same inputs always produce the same answer, which is what makes it worth
asking before a run exists.

It returns the *same* [`ContextPolicyDto`] a run carries, so a preview and
the thing it previewed cannot describe a policy differently.

200.description: The policy those inputs resolve to

422.description: A value outside the closed set, or a seed reaching an explicit-only class

get.summary: The durable control-plane feed.
get.description:
Three properties make it restartable. Every frame's SSE `id` is the event's
own persisted control-plane cursor, so `Last-Event-ID` is a position this
Realm actually allocated. Delivery is strictly greater than the requested
position, so nothing is repeated and nothing is skipped. And the events come
from SQLite rather than from memory, so a reconnect after a restart reads the
same log the previous connection was reading.

200.description: An SSE stream of control-plane events

410.description: The position is outside the retained history

post.summary: Settle one run against what its runtime reports right now.
post.description:
The request body is empty and stays empty. Kontor loads the run's immutable
binding, asks the runtime that issued it for a fresh `inspect`, persists what
came back, and only then asks whether that observation is allowed to close the
run — a question answered by the binding's *frozen* trust grade, not by
anything the caller said. An operator who could post an outcome would be
closing a run on their own authority while it looked like the runtime's, which
is the one thing a control plane must never let happen quietly.

Idempotent: a run that is already closed reports its stored closure and no
second observation is taken.

409.description: The binding no longer names a session this runtime will act on

422.description: The runtime does not evidence a terminal state

503.description: The runtime could not be reached

post.summary: Settle one bounded Kontor role turn.
post.description:

the fleet. It closes the **turn**, never the run: the seat's native session
stays live and reusable, and nothing here is admissible as evidence that the
runtime ended anything.

post.summary: Append one gate verdict.
post.description:
The gate is the addressed resource and `record` is the action, so the action
is its own path segment rather than a `:record` suffix on the identifier. That
is also the only encoding a router can express — a segment holds one parameter
*or* a literal, never both — so the two agree, and no action is smuggled into
a query parameter where it would escape the route contract.

The tier is decided by the *verdict*, not by the route: an ordinary pass or
rejection is operator work, and waiving a gate is a decision about whether the
rule applies at all, which is admin authority.

post.summary: Ask one seat to compact its context, in place.
post.description:
Every guard the approved policy names runs **before** the adapter is
reached, and each of them refuses without an effect:

* realm authorization and a frozen binding, from [`resolve`];
* the runtime's frozen [`RuntimeCapability::Compact`] capability, so a
  `required` policy on a runtime that cannot compact refuses here rather
  than being reported as done;
* a *deterministic* trigger — threshold, durable scope boundary or an
  authorized operator request. A finished role turn is not one, and there is
  no spelling for it in [`CompactionTrigger`];
* no active tool action and no unresolved permission, because compacting
  mid-decision discards the decision;
* a sealed durable handoff for a boundary or operator compaction, plus the
  Context Pack hash the run was frozen against.

The `Idempotency-Key` *is* the compaction receipt id, for the same reason it
is the message id on `send_message`: two tokens could disagree about whether
a retry is the same attempt, and only one of them is what the ledger keys on.

200.description: The outcome, or the original receipt replayed

409.description: The id already recorded a different attempt

422.description: An unsafe trigger, a missing handoff, or a runtime that cannot compact

post.summary: Deliver one message into a session.
post.description:
The `Idempotency-Key` *is* the stable client message id: it must parse as one,
and it is what the runtime's own ledger keys the effect on. Requiring two
separate tokens would create two things that can disagree about whether a
retry is the same message, and only one of them would be the one the runtime
actually checks.

200.description: Delivered, or the original ack replayed

409.description: The id already committed different content

get.summary: Follow a session's content strictly after a validated timeline anchor.
get.description:
The anchor is required, and that is the transport spelling of "history anchors
live": without a position a previous read validated, there is nothing for
delivery to be strictly after, and a stream that guessed would be unable to
tell a runtime dropping events from its own missing start.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The anchor a timeline read returned

200.description: An SSE stream of session content

get.summary: One page of a session's recorded content, read from the runtime.
get.description:
The page is validated through `HistoryReader` before it is returned, so what a
caller receives is exactly-once by construction: a redelivered item is dropped
from the page rather than merely uncounted, and a page that changes epoch,
skips a sequence or rewrites a position it already delivered is refused.

409.description: The timeline must be refetched from the start

AccountProfileDto.description:
One provider-account profile, with nothing a caller could authenticate with.

The credential reference is an opaque alias whose meaning lives entirely in
the resolver's policy: publishing it discloses nothing, and there is no field
here that a token, a config home or a keychain target could occupy.

AppliedDto.description:
Whether an ensure/apply wrote the row or found it already matching.

It is on every item of every declarative answer, because "it worked" and "it
was already like that" are different facts and a caller reconciling a plan
needs to tell them apart without diffing.

AppliedEpicDto.description: One epic after it was applied.

bundle_hash.description:
A stable digest of the graph this call applied.

It covers the *content* — the epic and its revision, the pinned profile
and team revisions, and every task's identity, title, state, dependency
set and ticket links — and nothing about the call that applied it. So a
byte-identical reapply of an unchanged graph returns the same digest, and
a caller diffing it to detect drift sees drift only when the graph
actually moved.

It is deliberately *not* the resolved bundle's digest: that one covers the
resolution, including when it happened, and therefore differs on every
call. Reporting it here made drift detection fire on every replay.

no window in which a task exists without the workflow it will be judged
against.

The budget bounds an arming decision authorizes.

Every bound is mandatory and positive. There is no "unlimited": a bound that
could be omitted would read as "no work allowed" in one place and "no ceiling"
in another, and arming is exactly where that ambiguity is unaffordable.

What a caller states when asking a seat to compact.

The safe-point facts are stated by the caller because only the operator
driving the session knows them; the guard refuses on either, so stating them
honestly is the caller's obligation and stating them at all is mandatory.

ConnectorSpecDto.description:
One connector specification revision this build can serve.

`installed` distinguishes "this deployment ships the mapping" from "this
project pinned it": a bundled revision nothing installed is selectable, and a
task linked to a ticket it does not cover is exactly the unmapped link
`ticket:reconcile-plan` already reports rather than silently converging.

field mapping covers, or the semantic milestones a workflow mapping does.

ContextPolicyDto.description:
One seat's context-window policy and the latest attempt to compact it.

The single projection API, CLI and MCP all render, so the three cannot drift
into describing the same seat differently. Every field is provider-neutral:
no configuration key, no daemon payload, no prompt and no credential appears
here, and a runtime that measures nothing reports nothing rather than zero.

capability.description: Whether the runtime could be told at all.

clamp.description: Why the effective trigger differs from the requested one.

effective_tokens.description:
The trigger actually in force. Absent for `native`, and absent when the
runtime cannot be configured at all.

enforcement.description: How hard the runtime was required to honour it.

oneOf.description: The most recent compaction attempt, if there has been one.

minimum_trigger_tokens.description: The smallest trigger the runtime can take, when it declared one.

permits_reuse.description: Whether this seat may be reused without waiting for a confirmation.

requested_class.description: The class that was asked for.

requested_tokens.description: The trigger that class asks for. Absent for `native`.

safe_ceiling_tokens.description:
The runtime ceiling the request was measured against, when it declared
one. Absence is unknown.

source.description: Which declaration the policy came from.

trigger_scope.description: What the trigger is measured against.

What a caller asks the preview to resolve.

Explicit inputs only. The preview is a pure function of what is stated here,
so two callers stating the same thing always get the same answer — which is
what makes it usable for "what would this seat get" before anything exists.

minimum_trigger.description: The smallest trigger that runtime can take, when it attests one.

The policy the team template's role slot declares, if it declares one.
The policy an authorized run override would carry, if there is one.

EnsureAccountProfileRequest.description:
What `provider-account-profiles:ensure` is asked for.

The label is the stable caller key. Only the two mutable fields a profile has
are settable here; everything credential-affecting is immutable for the life
of a profile, which is why rotation is a new profile rather than an edit.

credential_alias.description:
The approved credential alias the resolver looks the credential up under.
An alias is not a capability: one the resolver policy does not already
approve resolves to nothing.

harness.description: The runtime family this account authenticates against.

label.description: Human label. The natural identity inside the project.

EnsureProjectRequest.description:
What `projects:ensure` is asked for.

`root_path` is the stable caller key: it is unique across the database and
immutable once the project exists, so the same request always resolves to the
same project without a second identity that could disagree with it.

name.description: Human name. Immutable once the project exists.

root_path.description: Canonical absolute root path. The natural identity.

workflow_revision.description:
The revision a gate recording must present.

It is the *workflow's* revision, not the task's: a gate verdict is checked
against the workflow that pins the profile declaring the gate, and the two
aggregates move independently. Reporting it here is what makes the gate
list above actionable — a caller that had to guess it would be right only
until the first phase advance.

`None` when the task has no active workflow, which is also when `gates` is
empty: there is no revision to present because there is nothing to record
a verdict against.

Where its work happens. `None` is why a task cannot be seated, so it is
reported rather than left to be discovered at admission.

EpicTaskRequest.description:
One task in a declarative epic.

`title` is the stable caller key: dependencies name it, a reapply matches on
it, and it is immutable for the life of the task.

depends_on.description: The titles of the sibling tasks that must finish first.

module.description: The module the task contends for, if any.

title.description: The title, which is this task's identity inside the epic.

worktree.description:
The absolute path this task's work happens in.

It is the task's *placement*, and admission has nowhere else to learn it
from: a seat is a session opened in a directory, and a control plane with
no field for one either refuses to seat or invents a path — which is
deciding where code gets edited by string formatting.

Omitting it leaves any previously declared worktree alone rather than
clearing it. A task that has never had one cannot be seated, and says so.

One gate the pinned profile declares, and what discharging it needs.

The declared authority travels with the state on purpose. A Lead driving a
task to closure has to know *who* may evaluate each gate and *which* artifacts
it requires, and a projection that reported only a state would make that
knowable solely by reading the profile pack out of band — which is exactly the
out-of-band step the public API exists to remove.

The closed set of lifecycle transitions a Lead may ask for.

One endpoint and an enum rather than six routes: the transitions share every
input — an expected revision, a reason, the evidence the domain demands — and
splitting them would make it possible for one to drift out of agreement with
the transition table the others are judged by.

response_id.description: The Kontor identifier the answer was sent under.

sequence.description: Where it landed inside that epoch.

PermissionRequestBody.description: How a permission request is answered.

ProfileArtifactDto.description: One artifact contract a work profile declares.

evidence_required.description: Whether stored evidence is required, not merely a declaration.

ProfileHandoffDto.description: One declared handoff of the team a profile prescribes.

after_phase.description: The phase after which the handoff may happen.

from_slot.description: The slot that hands work over.

required_artifacts.description: The artifacts the receiving slot needs before it may start.

ProfilePackDto.description: One profile pack this Realm can resolve a category from.

applied.description: Whether this call registered it, for a register.

categories.description: The categories it advertises, in manifest order.

document_hash.description:
The digest of the canonical document. `None` for the compiled pack, which
is not stored as a document.

source.description: Whether it is compiled into this build or was registered by an operator.

ProfilePhaseDto.description: One phase of a work profile, as the catalog spells it.

gates.description: Gates evaluated at the end of it.

rejection_route.description: Where rejected work returns to, when the profile routes it.

required_artifacts.description: Artifacts that must exist before the phase can complete.

ProfileValidationDto.description:
What validating a work-profile category proved.

A validation answers about the *pack*, not about a request: it re-runs the
pack's own invariants and re-derives the bundle digest. There is no field
here a caller could supply a profile through — validating something the
deployment does not ship would prove nothing about what it will run.

availability.description:
Whether the category is backed by a profile revision, or advertises
vocabulary only. A manifest-only category is deliberately not runnable.

bundle_hash.description: The bundle digest, when it resolved.

bundle_verified.description:
Whether the category resolves to a bundle that verifies against its own
pinned digests.

refused.description: Why validation failed, when it did. A rule, never a stored value.

ProjectDto.description: One project, as a bootstrap caller sees it.

realm_id.description: The Realm it belongs to.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

ProjectionDto.description: The orthogonal state of one run, plus how old its newest confirmation is.

derived.description: What Kontor concluded. `terminal` carries its outcome separately.

freshness.description:
How old that confirmation is, judged against the daemon's evidence window
at the instant this snapshot was taken.

last_confirmed_at.description: When the newest trusted confirmation arrived.

last_cursor.description: The control-plane position of the newest reduced event.

outcome.description: The outcome, when the run is closed.

ProvenanceDto.description: Where one resolved value came from.

layer.description: The layer that last wrote it.

path.description: The JSON pointer the value sits at.

ReadyTaskDto.description: One task the planner would admit, and what it would run under.

account_profile_id.description: The account profile it is pinned to, if any.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family it would run on.

realm_id.description: The Realm.

schema_version.description: The envelope contract it was created under.

ReceiptDto.description: The durable record of one command.

attempts.description: How many dispatch attempts have been made.

state.description: How far it has got. An acknowledgement is never a completion.

target_revision.description: The revision the intent was computed against.

replayed.description:
`true` when the idempotency key had already recorded this exact command,
so nothing was written and the original receipt is being returned.

ReceiptResponse.description: A receipt, and whether this call is the one that recorded it.

evaluator_role.description: The role recording it. Checked against the pinned profile's authority.

evidence.description:
The artifacts cited. A pass or a waiver requires the ones the profile
declares.

expected_revision.description: The revision the caller read the task's workflow at.

reviewer_principal.description:
The stable authenticated principal recording it.

Omitting it records the verdict and attributes it to nobody; it never
silently falls back to the run or the display name.

verdict.description: The verdict. `waived` is an admin decision; the rest are operator work.

RedactionDto.description:
One member the resolver removed, and why.

It carries the path and the reason and never the value, not even its length:
a redaction record that described what it removed would be the disclosure it
exists to prevent.

path.description: The JSON pointer that was removed.

source_id.description: The source that declared the redaction.

RegisterPackRequest.description:
What `catalog/packs:register` is asked for.

The whole pack, as a document. It is one operation and not two — "register a
profile" and "register a team template" — because a work profile prescribes a
team, pins role and skill revisions, and cannot be resolved without them: a
profile admitted alone would be a catalogue entry that refuses to resolve, and
a team admitted alone would be one nothing can select.

pack.description: The pack document. Validated in full before anything is stored.

snapshot.description:
Whether to freeze the resolution onto the task's live run.

A preview reads and returns nothing durable. A snapshot needs a run to
belong to, because a frozen context pack is evidence about *what a run was
given* and a pack belonging to no run is evidence about nothing.

ResolvedContextDto.description:
What resolving a task's Context Pack produced.

The resolved document itself is deliberately absent. What a caller needs from
this operation is *determinism and accountability* — the same inputs produce
the same hash, and every path is attributable — and shipping the merged
content back would make this the one route through which everything the
resolver was given leaves the process.

agent_run_id.description: The agent run the snapshot belongs to, when there is one.

context_hash.description: The digest of the canonical resolved document.

context_pack_id.description: The frozen pack, when this call snapshotted one.

provenance.description: Where every resolved path came from.

realm_id.description: The Realm it was resolved in.

task_id.description: The task it was resolved for.

RevisionRefDto.description: One immutable specification revision, as a caller pins it.

applied.description: Whether this call recorded it or replayed one.

authorized_by_role.description: The role it is attributed to.

disposition.description:
Always `waived`. Spelled out rather than implied, and closed: there is no
second disposition a caller may select.

evidence_hash.description: The canonical digest the closure re-derives.

realm_id.description: The Realm it was recorded in.

team_run_closed.description:
The team run this waiver closed, when it was the last slot outstanding.
`null` while any other declared slot is still unaccounted for.

team_run_id.description: The team run whose slot was excused.

RunDto.description: One agent run, as a cross-boundary reader sees it.

account_profile_id.description: The coding account it is pinned to, if any.

applied.description: The team template revision this run's team pinned.

oneOf.description: The context window this seat was launched under, once it has been frozen.

parent_agent_run_id.description: The run it succeeds, for recovery and resume.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

RuntimeCapabilityDto.description:
What one configured runtime family can currently prove.

The family is a *name*, never an endpoint: there is no field here a URL, a
port or a client configuration could occupy.

account_env.description:
Whether it can prove which coding account a run executes as. Paseo 1.0
reports `false`, which is why a per-run account pin against it is refused
rather than silently ignored.

max_concurrent_sessions.description: Largest number of simultaneous native sessions.

max_message_bytes.description: Largest message body it accepts, in bytes.

reachable.description:
Whether the family answered discovery at all. A family that could not be
reached reports its absence rather than a plausible capability set.

supported.description: The operations it declares, in a stable order.

trust_grade.description: How much of what it reports Kontor may act on.

RuntimeSettlementDto.description:
What settling one run against its runtime produced.

Nothing in the request shapes this. There is no field on the way in for a
verdict, a terminal state, an evidence hash or a citation, which is the point:
settlement is Kontor *asking* a runtime what is true and recording the answer,
and an operator who could supply any of those would be closing a run on their
own authority while it looked like the runtime's.

applied.description: Whether this call closed the run, or found it already closed.

evidence_cursor.description:
The control-plane position of the observation the closure cites.

It is a position in this Realm's own log, so the closure points at
evidence the store can re-load and re-prove rather than at a digest the
caller handed over.

observed.description: What the runtime reported the session is doing, right now.

outcome.description: How the run closed, when the observation qualified to close it.

realm_id.description: The Realm it happened in.

receipt_id.description: The command receipt that authorizes the settlement.

team_pending.description:
Why the team is not closed yet, when it is not. A static rule, never a
stored value.

team_run_closed.description:
The team run, once every declared role slot is terminal and the team's
closure has been certified.

SchedulerPlanDto.description:
What the planner decided, and what it decided against.

A plan is a dry run in the strongest sense available: it reads rows, it calls
no runtime, and it writes nothing. `plan_hash` is what `scheduler:start`
applies, so a caller starts the plan it was shown rather than whatever the
world looks like by the time it decides.

authorizations.description: The arming decisions the plan was computed against.

blocked.description: The tasks that would not, with the reason for each.

plan_hash.description: The digest of the whole plan.

ready.description: The tasks that would be admitted, in admission order.

realm_id.description: The Realm it was planned in.

scheduling_open.description:
Whether startup reconciliation has finished. Nothing is admitted until it
has, and a plan taken before it says so.

blocked.description: The tasks the plan named that admission then refused, with the reason.

realm_id.description: The Realm it was started in.

SeatProjectionDto.description: One seat: a role slot, the run filling it and the native session behind it.

attached.description: Whether this process still holds the frozen capability snapshot for it.

native_id.description: The runtime's own session id. Correlation evidence, never identity.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family that owns the session, if the run is bound.

realm_id.description: The Realm it happened in.

receipt_id.description: The command receipt that authorizes it.

oneOf.description: The team revision that profile pins.

SelectionRequest.description:
What a selection-correction operation is asked for.

One request shape for all three corrections, because they are the same
decision about three different pins and splitting them would let one drift out
of agreement with the pre-run rule the others obey.

account_profile_id.description: The provider-account profile to pin, for an account correction.

expected_revision.description: The revision the caller read the task at.

reason.description: Why the correction is being made. Recorded, never interpreted.

oneOf.description:
The team revision the caller believes the profile pins, for a team
correction.

work_profile_category.description: The work-profile category to pin, for a profile correction.

SettleTurnRequest.description:
What `turns:settle` is asked for.

It settles **Kontor's** bounded turn in a persistent seat. There is no field
here for a runtime verdict, a terminal state or a native observation, and
that is the point: a seat is expected to still be sitting there when this
returns, ready for its next turn. Whether the *session* ever ended is a
separate question only the runtime can answer, and `runtime:settle` is where
it is asked.

expected_task_revision.description: The task revision the caller believes is current.

role_slot.description: The role slot whose turn this is.

SettledTurnDto.description: What settling one bounded role turn produced.

account_profile.description:
The provider account the seat runs as, derived from the bound run rather
than supplied by the caller. Operational context, never attribution.

agent_run_id.description: The seat's agent run, which stays open.

applied.description: Whether this call settled it, or replayed a settlement.

binding_generation.description: The native binding generation the seat was bound under.

evidence_hash.description: The digest it was settled under.

follow_ups.description: The follow-ups this settlement derived, in slot order.

realm_id.description: The Realm it was settled in.

seat_live.description:
Whether the seat's native session is still live. Settling a turn must
never end one, so this is the assertion that it did not.

settled_by.description:
The tier the settling caller authenticated at. Not a claimed identity:
it is what the presented credential proved.

team_run_closed.description:
The team run, once every declared slot has settled its final turn and the
team's closure was certified from those rows. `None` while any slot is
still unaccounted for.

turn_ordinal.description: Its position in that seat's sequence of turns.

SnapshotDto_RunDto.description:
A point-in-time value and the position it is consistent with.

It is the wire spelling of `kontor-core`'s own `SnapshotEnvelope`: a
subscriber resumes strictly after `snapshot_cursor`, in the same Realm.

realm_id.description: The Realm this snapshot came from.

snapshot_cursor.description: The position it is consistent with.

value.description: One agent run, as a cross-boundary reader sees it.

account_profile_id.description: The coding account it is pinned to, if any.

applied.description: The team template revision this run's team pinned.

oneOf.description: The context window this seat was launched under, once it has been frozen.

parent_agent_run_id.description: The run it succeeds, for recovery and resume.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

SnapshotDto_TaskDto.description:
A point-in-time value and the position it is consistent with.

It is the wire spelling of `kontor-core`'s own `SnapshotEnvelope`: a
subscriber resumes strictly after `snapshot_cursor`, in the same Realm.

realm_id.description: The Realm this snapshot came from.

snapshot_cursor.description: The position it is consistent with.

value.description: One task, its active workflow and the gates reduced from its evaluations.

applied.description: The pinned specification revisions in force.

current_phase.description: The phase the active workflow is in.

gates.description: The gate states, keyed by gate.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

plan_hash.description:
The plan digest a previous `scheduler:plan` returned. A plan that no
longer describes the Realm is refused rather than re-derived, because the
caller authorized *that* batch and not whatever replaced it.

StartedSeatDto.description: One seat the start actually produced.

agent_run_id.description: The agent run filling the role slot.

applied.description:
Whether this call created the seat, or found the runtime already holding
one for that `(team run, role slot)` and reused it.

native_id.description: The runtime's own session id. Correlation evidence, never identity.

runtime_kind.description: The runtime family that owns the session.

task_id.description: The task the seat is working on.

team_run_id.description: The team run the scheduler created or reused.

StreamFrameDto.description:
One frame of live session content.

The item is wrapped rather than sent bare so that *every* frame of the stream
carries the Realm and the run it belongs to — a console holding two sessions
open must never have to infer which one a frame came from.

agent_run_id.description: The run whose session produced it.

realm_id.description: The Realm the session belongs to.

StreamRefusalDto.description:
A frame the live-content stream emits instead of an item when the timeline can
no longer be followed.

realm_id.description: The Realm the session belongs to.

rule.description: A static description of what broke.

SubmitIntakeRequest.description:
What `intake:submit` is asked for.

The envelope is the *canonical* event, already redacted by whoever holds the
connection: this operation evaluates it and records the decision, and there is
no field here for a verdict, an approval or a work graph. What a matched event
becomes is the trigger's decision, not the submitter's.

external_event_id.description: The event id as the source system spells it.

external_observed_at.description: When the source system observed it.

TaskDto.description: One task, its active workflow and the gates reduced from its evaluations.

applied.description: The pinned specification revisions in force.

current_phase.description: The phase the active workflow is in.

gates.description: The gate states, keyed by gate.

revision.description: The revision a write must present.

TeamRunProjectionDto.description: One team run and its seats, as the epic projection reports them.

seats.description: One entry per agent run the scheduler admitted into a role slot.

definition_hash.description: The digest of its canonical definition.

slots.description: The role slots it seats, in declaration order.

TicketClaimDto.description:
What claiming one task's tickets would do, and did.

The action is always [`OwnershipAction::ReassignToPrincipal`] as the domain
spells it — there is no field on the way in for an assignee, so a caller can
claim a ticket for the principal Kontor authenticates as and for nobody else.

action.description: The ownership action, as the domain names it.

realm_id.description: The Realm it happened in.

receipt_id.description: The command receipt that authorizes it.

TicketCommentDto.description:
One mirrored inbound comment revision.

The body is deliberately absent and only its digest is reported. A comment is
mirrored so Kontor can prove *that* it saw a revision and in what order; a
read that also handed the prose back would make this the place ticket content
leaves the process, which is the disclosure the mirror exists to avoid.

body_hash.description: The digest of the body. Never the body.

external_comment_id.description: The comment id as the external system spells it.

external_created_at.description: When the external system says it was created.

external_updated_at.description: When the external system says it was last updated.

link_id.description: The ticket link it arrived on.

supersedes.description: The revision this one edits, when it is an edit.

TicketCommentPullDto.description: What pulling one task's inbound comments produced.

held.description: How many revisions the task holds after the pull.

mirrored.description: How many revisions this pull mirrored. A replay mirrors none.

realm_id.description: The Realm it happened in.

receipt_id.description: The command receipt that authorizes it.

TicketConflictDto.description:
One recorded reconciliation conflict.

A conflict names its *kind* and the observation it was raised from, and
carries neither the external value that disagreed nor the comment that
mentioned it. The kind is what a human acts on; the values are what the
connector holds.

link_id.description: The ticket link it was raised on.

observation_id.description: The observation it was raised from.

resolved_at.description: When it was resolved, when it has been.

spec_version.description: The specification revision it was judged against.

task_revision.description: The task revision at the time it was raised.

TicketFieldDiffDto.description:
One typed field difference between Kontor and an external ticket.

The set of fields is closed by the pinned field specification: there is no
member here that could carry an arbitrary status, an assignee or a comment.

external.description: What the external system last reported, when there is an observation.

kontor.description: What Kontor believes, as the pinned mapping spells it.

milestone.description: The semantic milestone the field maps to.

TicketLinkRequest.description: One external ticket an applied task is linked to.

connector.description: The connector implementation. Never its vendor semantics.

TicketReconcileAppliedDto.description: What applying a ticket reconciliation produced.

realm_id.description: The Realm it happened in.

receipt_id.description: The command receipt that authorizes it.

TicketReconcilePlanDto.description: What reconciling one task's tickets would do.

converged.description: Whether every link is already converged.

realm_id.description: The Realm it was planned in.

TimelineDto.description: One page of a session's recorded content.

agent_run_id.description: The run whose session was read.

anchor.description:
The cursor a live subscription resumes from. The same position as
`end_epoch`/`end_sequence`, in the form `/stream` accepts.

end_epoch.description:
The last position this page covers. A live subscription must start
strictly after it.

end_sequence.description: The sequence half of that position.

epoch.description: The runtime's content epoch every item belongs to.

items.description: The items, in ascending sequence order.

next.description: Where to continue, or `null` when the history is exhausted.

realm_id.description: The Realm the session belongs to.

message_id.description: The Kontor message id, when the item is about one.

native_event_id.description: The runtime's own event id, when it provides one.

payload.description: The runtime's own payload. Never persisted by this control plane.

permission_id.description: The runtime's permission request id, when the item is about one.

TriggerSpecDto.description:
One pinned trigger revision, as an operator reads it back.

The filter clauses and the dedup pointers are reported as *pointers*, never
with the values a matching event carried: a trigger is configuration, and an
event's contents belong to the event.

auto_arm.description:
Whether it may arm the work it creates without a human, as the pinned
policy spells it.

dedup_pointers.description: The envelope pointers its dedup key is derived from.

event_schema.description: The event schema it accepts, at its pinned revision.

filter_pointers.description: The envelope pointers its filter constrains.

source_connection.description: The configured connection of that kind.

source_kind.description: The source kind it listens to.

work_profile.description: The work profile revision the work it proposes would use.

TurnFollowUpDto.description: One follow-up a settled turn derived.

after_phase.description: Why it was derived: the handoff's phase and artifact conditions are met.

dispatched.description: Whether the effect actually reached the seat.

target_agent_run_id.description: The seat it reached, when one was materialized for that slot.

to_role_slot.description: The slot the work was handed to.

WaiveRoleSlotRequest.description:
Excuse one declared role slot that was never bound to a session.

What this body deliberately does **not** carry is the design: no
`agent_run_id`, no binding or runtime identity, no outcome or lifecycle, no
`terminal: true`, no generic disposition kind, no caller credential. A waiver
is a statement about a *slot* and the template's own permission to omit it —
every one of those omitted fields would turn it into a statement about a
session or a run that nothing observed.

authorized_by_role.description:
The role the waiver is attributed to. Policy attribution, checked against
the frozen slot's own policy — never a person, never the caller.

evidence.description: Every evidence reference the frozen policy demands, at least.

expected_team_revision.description: The team revision the caller believes is current.

WorkProfileCatalogDto.description:
One selectable work profile, as the catalog advertises it.

The revision is what a caller pins in `epics:apply`; the team it prescribes is
reported alongside it so a Lead can see the closure it is choosing rather than
discovering it at apply time.

bundle_hash.description: The digest of the whole resolved bundle. What `epics:apply` freezes.

category.description: The pack category this profile is advertised under.

profile.description: The profile revision the category resolves to.

oneOf.description: The team revision the profile pins, when it prescribes one.

WorkProfileDetailDto.description:
The whole of one selectable work profile, resolved.

It is the catalog entry plus everything a Lead would otherwise have had to
read the pack out of band to learn: the phase order, the gate authority, the
artifact contracts and the handoff DAG that decides which seat starts first.
Nothing here is per-project — a category resolves to the same bundle in every
Realm running this build, which is why it is a workspace-level read.

bundle_hash.description: The digest of the whole resolved bundle. What `epics:apply` freezes.

category.description: The pack category this profile is advertised under.

definition_hash.description:
The digest of the profile's canonical definition.

This is the stable one. `bundle_hash` covers the *resolution*, which
records when it happened, so two reads of an unchanged category answer
with two different bundle digests and the same definition digest. A
caller proving the pack has not moved compares this.

eligible_roots.description:
The role slots that no handoff feeds, which are the seats that start with
work rather than with an instruction to wait.

entry_phase.description: The phase the profile enters at.

gates.description: Every gate it declares, with the authority and evidence each one names.

handoffs.description: The declared handoffs of the team it pins.

phases.description: The phases it declares, in declaration order.

profile.description: The profile revision the category resolves to.

oneOf.description: The team revision the profile pins, when it prescribes one.

terminal_phases.description: The phases it may terminate at.

realm_bearer.description: One of the realm's tier secrets, read from its 0600 credential file.
